QuestionStmt.S: Which from following tests confirms presence of aldehyde group in glucose?

Option1Stmt.S: Formation of oxime when reacted with $\mathrm{NH_2OH}$.

Option2Stmt.S: Formation of gluconic acid when reacted with $\mathrm{Br_2}$ water.

Option3Stmt.S: Formation of saccharic acid when glucose and gluconic acid treated with dil. $\mathrm{HNO_3}$.

Option4Stmt.S: Formation of penta acetate when treated with acetic anhydride.

Solution.S: Glucose contains an aldehyde group that can be oxidized to a blob:null/cf54977a-de0b-4fae-a602-fa54faea45a5carboxylic acid. Bromine water ($\mathrm{Br_2}$) is a mild oxidizing agent that selectively oxidizes the aldehyde group of glucose to gluconic acid. This reaction confirms the presence of the aldehyde group. Option A (oxime formation) confirms carbonyl group but not specifically aldehyde. Option C (saccharic acid) involves further oxidation of both ends. Option D (penta acetate) indicates presence of five hydroxyl groups, not aldehyde. Therefore, the correct answer is B.
